sections.name: Sell-Side Quality of Earnings and Institutional-Grade Financials

items.text: Capital Row provides M&A advisory and transaction preparation. Accounting, tax, legal, regulatory, compliance, valuation, attestation and other professional work is done by qualified third parties under their own engagements. A QoE is not an audit, a review, a valuation, or a guarantee of value or of closing. Capital Row arranges the sell-side Quality of Earnings with qualified, institutionally backed firms engaged separately. The QoE firm is responsible for its own method, findings and conclusions. Capital Row may supply deal context and proposed normalization items, and does not control the QoE firm's conclusions.

sections.name: Know the EBITDA a buyer can underwrite.

items.text: Know the EBITDA a buyer can underwrite.

A sell-side Quality of Earnings report is financial diligence done for the seller, before a buyer does its own. It asks whether reported earnings are accurate, what they are made of, whether they will recur and how much of them turns into cash, and it reconciles reported results to normalized EBITDA. It is analysis with support behind every adjustment, not a list of add-backs the owner hopes a buyer will accept.
What a sell-side QoE does for the owner

It shows the owner and the deal team the issues a private equity buyer, a strategic acquirer or a lender will raise, while there is still time to act. The owner then decides what to fix, what to document, what to disclose and how to tell the financial story before the business goes to market.

The work ties the financial statements back to the general ledger, the trial balance, bank statements, payroll, tax filings, customer and payer detail, operating systems and the contracts that matter. Any adjustment that moves value has its document in place before a buyer asks.

Bookkeeping keeps the record. A sell-side QoE reads that record as a buyer will. Does revenue repeat? Do margins hold? Does an expense really end at closing? Is there enough working capital? Which liabilities count as debt? Can a new owner earn the same result?

The seller's report sets an open, documented starting point. The buyer's report is paid for by the buyer, to support its case and to find what could go wrong. Buyers and lenders may still commission their own work, and a prepared seller meets it with reconciled schedules, written positions and an organized way to answer, rather than a blank page.
Nothing here is about hiding weaknesses. Each one is found, sized, explained and, where it can be, fixed before it becomes a lever in the buyer's hands.

Preparation is Capital Row's own first pass, done before the full report. We trace reported earnings to source documents and mark each adjustment supported or unsupported. It is not a quality of earnings report, and it does not replace one.
What is a sell-side Quality of Earnings report?
Transaction-focused financial diligence prepared for the seller before going to market. It reconciles reported results to normalized EBITDA and documents the evidence behind each material adjustment.
Why should the seller commission a QoE before the buyer does?
Issues found before the letter of intent can be fixed, explained or priced on your terms. Issues found after it are negotiated while the buyer holds exclusivity.
How is sell-side QoE different from buy-side QoE?
The seller's report sets a documented starting point. The buyer's report is paid for by the buyer, to support its own case and to look for what could go wrong. A buyer may still commission one.
Is a Quality of Earnings report an audit?
No. It is analysis prepared for a transaction. It is not an audit, a review, a compilation, a valuation or an assurance opinion.
Does a sell-side QoE raise the price?

It does not change what the business earned, and no outcome is guaranteed. It shows how much of the earnings can be supported, and it brings out early the issues that often lead to price changes late in a deal.
Reported EBITDA adjusted for items that do not reflect the ongoing business: one-time, nonoperating, owner-specific and misclassified items, each with support.

Adjustments for costs or income that will not continue under a new owner and that can be documented, such as above-market owner compensation, personal expenses and one-time professional fees. An add-back without evidence is unlikely to hold up when a buyer reviews it.
What is a net working-capital peg and why does it matter?
It is the level of working capital the seller agrees to deliver at closing. If working capital at closing is below the peg, the price is usually adjusted down by the difference.
Obligations a buyer treats like debt and deducts from the price, such as unpaid taxes, deferred compensation, accrued bonuses, customer deposits and some leases.
What if my books are cash-basis, tax-basis or out of date?
Yes. Part of the work is converting material activity to accrual schedules a transaction can use and reconciling the records to source.

Usually three years of P&Ls and balance sheets, this year to date and the trailing twelve months, the general ledger, tax returns, bank statements, payroll records and the main contracts. The full data request is agreed when the work is scoped.
How long does the process take?
It depends on the size of the business, the number of entities and systems, and the condition of the records. The schedule is set with you after the first review.
Before you go to market, and early enough to fix what the work finds.
What if the QoE finds a problem?
That is the reason to do it first. The finding is sized, and you decide whether to correct it, document it or disclose it before a buyer sees it.
Do buyers rely on a QoE the seller paid for?
Buyers and lenders may still do their own diligence. A QoE performed by an independent firm, with schedules tied to source records, gives them a documented starting point.
Data is collected through a secure process, kept in a controlled working-file environment and released in stages. Sensitive records can be redacted or limited to a clean team.
How is the project fee handled?
The fee for the QoE is agreed in writing with the firm that performs it, before the work begins.
Is AI used in Quality of Earnings work?

Increasingly, yes, mostly to read and organize documents faster. Used well, it shortens extraction and reconciliation time. It does not replace source documents or professional judgment. Our own financial preparation starts with repeatable calculations and evidence that can be traced to its source, and advisers lead the last mile. Technology creates capacity. Human expertise turns that capacity into trusted advice.
What is the difference between deterministic and probabilistic AI?

A deterministic system gives the same answer every time from the same inputs, the way a formula does. A probabilistic system, including the large language models behind most AI tools, produces its most likely answer, and that answer can change from one run to the next. In diligence the difference matters. A number in an earnings bridge has to come out the same way every time and tie to a document.
What is agentic AI, and does it belong in diligence?

Agentic AI is software that plans and carries out a series of steps by itself, such as collecting files, matching records and drafting requests. It is useful for the routine work of gathering and organizing. It should not decide what counts as an adjustment or what a finding means. Those calls stay with accountable professionals.
What makes an AI-assisted solution qualified for this work?

Ask five questions of any provider. Does every figure trace to a source document? Are the calculations deterministic, so the same inputs give the same result? Are probabilistic tools limited to reading, sorting and flagging, with a person reviewing what they produce? Does your data stay in a secure environment, and is it kept out of the training of outside models? Is a named professional accountable for the conclusions?
